FirstFlip Business API (2026-11-02)

Download OpenAPI specification:

URL: https://firstflip.ng License: LicenseRef-FirstFlip-Docs

Accept crypto payments, create reusable payment links, and receive signed webhooks.

The FirstFlip Business API lets a business accept payments and build on FirstFlip programmatically. It is a JSON, resource-oriented HTTP API: predictable paths, Bearer secret-key auth, an Idempotency-Key on every write, cursor pagination, and one canonical error shape.

FirstFlip developer portal (guides, quickstart, SDKs, Postman collection)

Base URL & versioning

All paths are prefixed with /v1 (the version is in the path; a breaking change means /v2, additive changes stay in /v1). The sandbox base URL is https://api.firstflip.ng/v1.

Test mode only. Every endpoint runs in TEST MODE. No real money moves. Use your ffk_test_… secret key. Live mode is not yet enabled; a live key returns 403 live_mode_unavailable on money endpoints, and the same code you write against the sandbox will work unchanged when live mode opens.

One surface is ahead of that rule: /v1/cards answers a live key leg by leg instead of with one blanket refusal. Listing, retrieval, freeze and unfreeze already run live, and every leg that would move or release money — including the transaction statement list — returns 403 live_precondition_unmet with the missing rail named in error.param; see the Cards tag. Nothing else in /v1 has that wiring yet.

Authentication

Send your secret key as a bearer token on every request to a non-public endpoint:

Authorization: Bearer $FIRSTFLIP_SECRET_KEY

A secret key looks like ffk_test_… (test) or ffk_live_… (live). It is shown once, when it is created, and only its hash is stored — if you lose it, rotate it. The key is the sole source of identity: FirstFlip resolves the owning business from the key, so there is no account id to send and no way to act for another business. Keep secret keys server-side; never ship one in a browser, mobile app, or public repository. You mint and revoke keys yourself over the session-authenticated POST /api/business/developer/keys (a screen for it is still to come — during the beta, ask FirstFlip and we issue your test key over a private channel). There you choose the key's scopes and pin it to up to 20 exact ipAllowlist addresses.

Scopes

A key carries a scope list chosen when it is created. Every endpoint names the one scope it needs; a surface that both reads and writes has a pair:

Scope Endpoints
account:read GET /account
charges:read / charges:write charges: list/get, create, cancel, simulate payment
payment_links:read / payment_links:write payment links: list/get, create, deactivate
subaccounts:read / subaccounts:write sub-accounts: list/get, create, suspend, activate
cards:read / cards:write cards: list/get, issue, fund, withdraw, freeze/unfreeze, close, spend limits, simulate authorization, transactions
otps:read / otps:write OTP pricing/lookup, create, validate
fx:read / fx:write FX quotes and trades: get, create, simulate
virtual_accounts:read / virtual_accounts:write virtual accounts: get/list batch, create, bulk, deactivate, simulate payment
verifications:read / verifications:write BVN and bank-account verification, simulate
transfers:read / transfers:write transfers (payouts): list/get, create, bulk, get batch, simulate
assistant:ask POST /assistant

Every operation that requires a scope declares it as x-required-scope, so a tool can choose the right key without mapping this table by hand.

Send scopes when creating a key to mint a least-privilege credential — a checkout widget only needs payment_links:write, a reconciliation job only needs charges:read, a payout service only needs transfers:write. A key created without a scope list (including every key that predates scopes) can do everything its mode allows. An endpoint the key's scopes don't cover returns 403 insufficient_scope, which names the scope it wanted. Scopes are never widened after creation: rotate a key that needs more access.

Idempotency

Every POST that creates or changes something requires an Idempotency-Key header: a unique string you generate (a UUID v4 is ideal), up to 255 characters. If a request is interrupted, safely retry it with the same key — FirstFlip replays the original response (with Idempotent-Replayed: true) instead of acting twice. Reusing a key with a different body is rejected with 422 idempotency_key_reused. A request still in flight returns 409 idempotency_in_progress; retry it. Keys are scoped to your business and mode and expire after 24 hours. (POST /assistant and the public hosted pages do not take an idempotency key.)

Pagination

List endpoints return { "object": "list", "data": [ … ], "has_more": true|false }, newest first. Page with limit (1–100, default 20) and starting_after=<id of the last item>. Paging is stable: even when many records share a timestamp (a bulk payout writes its whole batch at once), following starting_after never skips or repeats an item.

Every list also takes a created_from / created_before window (RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC). It is half-open — created_from inclusive, created_before exclusive — so created_from=2026-11-04&created_before=2026-11-05 is exactly that UTC day, and walking consecutive windows counts every object once.

Errors

Every error — including malformed JSON, auth failures, rate limits and outages — uses one shape:

{ "error": { "type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "invalid_parameter",
             "message": "currency must be NGN or USD", "param": "currency" } }

type groups the failure, code is the stable machine-readable reason, message is human-readable, and param names the offending field when there is one (otherwise null).

Every response — success or failure, including 401, 404, 429 and 503 — also carries a Request-Id header: a UUID generated for that one request. A value you send is ignored, so an id quoted in a support ticket always names a request we can find. Include it when you contact us about an error. Every response is also marked Cache-Control: no-store: account data, balances and hosted pages must never sit in a shared or browser cache, where a stale page is worse than a failed one. The full catalog is x-error-codes below; the summary table:

HTTP type code retryable meaning
400 invalid_request_error invalid_json no Request body is not valid JSON
400 invalid_request_error invalid_parameter no A parameter is missing or invalid (see param)
400 invalid_request_error amount_too_small no amount is below the minimum charge
400 invalid_request_error insufficient_balance no A card does not hold the amount you asked to take off it
400 invalid_request_error question_required no Assistant: no question was sent
400 invalid_request_error question_too_long no Assistant: question exceeds 2000 characters
400 idempotency_error idempotency_key_required no Idempotency-Key header missing on a POST
401 authentication_error invalid_api_key no Key missing, malformed, revoked, or wrong mode
401 authentication_error key_expired no This key reached its expiry date; create or rotate a key
403 authentication_error ip_not_allowed no Caller IP is not on this key's allow-list
403 authentication_error business_inactive no The business that owns the key is not active
403 authentication_error insufficient_scope no This key was created without the scope the endpoint requires
403 invalid_request_error live_mode_unavailable no Live mode is not open yet; use a test key
403 invalid_request_error live_precondition_unmet no This live leg is waiting on a named platform rail; error.param says which one (cards only today)
404 invalid_request_error not_found no No such route
404 invalid_request_error resource_missing no No such charge/payment link for this key
409 invalid_request_error charge_not_pending no Charge is not in a state that allows this action
409 invalid_request_error subaccount_not_active no Sub-account is already suspended and cannot be suspended again
409 invalid_request_error subaccount_not_suspended no Sub-account is already active and cannot be activated again
409 invalid_request_error duplicate_reference no reference already used by this business (charges, sub-accounts, cards)
409 invalid_request_error card_closed no Card is closed — every action on it is refused, including unfreeze
409 invalid_request_error card_not_active no Card is frozen, so a withdrawal was refused; unfreeze it first
409 invalid_request_error card_limit_reached no This key already holds its 250 open cards; close one first
409 idempotency_error idempotency_in_progress yes A request with this key is still running; retry
413 invalid_request_error body_too_large no Request body exceeds the size limit
422 idempotency_error idempotency_key_reused no Key reused with a different request body
429 rate_limit_error rate_limited yes Too many requests; honor Retry-After
500 api_error internal_error yes Unexpected error on FirstFlip's side
503 api_error service_unavailable yes FirstFlip is briefly unavailable; see Retry-After
503 api_error rate_unavailable yes Exchange rates are briefly unavailable; retry
503 api_error assistant_disabled no The developer assistant is switched off
503 api_error assistant_unavailable yes The assistant is temporarily unavailable

Rate limits

Limits are enforced per secret key (and a per-IP backstop). On 429 the response carries Retry-After (seconds); authenticated responses also carry X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining. Current windows: reads 300/min, writes 60/min, assistant 30/hour, per-IP backstop 1200/min, hosted sandbox pages 30/min per IP. Retry a 429 after the stated delay, reusing the same Idempotency-Key on writes.

Webhooks

FirstFlip POSTs signed events to the endpoint(s) you register over POST /api/business/developer/webhooks. Verify the FirstFlip-Signature header over the raw request body before trusting a webhook — see the webhooks section.

Compliance

FirstFlip is registered (not licensed) and shows integer-free major-unit amounts with an explicit currency on every money field. Secrets are never logged. Partner/rail names never appear in any request, response, field, error, or webhook payload.

Account

Identify the business behind the current secret key.

Retrieve the current account

Returns the business tied to the secret key you sent, the key's mode, and the masked key. This is the ideal first call to confirm your credentials and environment.

bearerAuth

Charges

A one-time request for payment. Create it, share its hosted URL, and act on charge.paid.

Create a charge

Creates a one-time charge for an amount you set in major units. FirstFlip quotes the exact crypto amount the customer must pay (asset + network you chose, plus the receive fee) and returns a hosted_url where they complete payment. In test mode the pay address is a labelled TEST-… placeholder and payment is simulated — nothing moves money.

Requires an Idempotency-Key header. If you pass a reference, it must be unique within your business (a repeat returns 409 duplicate_reference).

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
header Parameters
Idempotency-Key
required
string <= 255 characters
Example: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-a0b1-c2d3e4f50617

A unique key you generate (e.g. a UUID v4), up to 255 characters. Required on every POST that creates or changes something. Retry a failed request with the same key to replay the original response instead of acting twice.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
amount
required
number > 0

The price in major units of currency, at most 2 decimal places. Must be at least the minimum charge (default 5 USD / 5000 NGN, configurable) and at most 1,000,000 USD or 1,000,000,000 NGN.

currency
required
string
Enum: "NGN" "USD"
pay_asset
string
Default: "USDT"
Enum: "USDT" "USDC" "BTC"

The asset the customer pays in.

pay_network
string
Enum: "trc20" "bep20" "bitcoin"

The network. Must be valid for pay_asset: USDT → trc20 or bep20 (default trc20); USDC → bep20 (default bep20); BTC → bitcoin (default bitcoin). Defaults to the asset's default network if omitted.

description
string <= 500 characters

Shown on the hosted pay page.

reference
string <= 100 characters

Your own order id. Must be unique within your business.

expires_in_minutes
integer [ 15 .. 10080 ]
Default: 60

How long the charge stays payable (15 minutes to 7 days).

object (Metadata) <= 20 properties

Up to 20 key/value pairs you attach to an object; echoed back on reads and in webhooks. Keys match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$. Values are stored as strings (numbers and booleans are coerced to strings) of at most 500 characters.

object (ChargeCustomer)

Optional customer details attached to a charge.

Responses

List charges

Returns your charges, newest first. Filter by status, reference or a created_from/created_before window.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
limit
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 20
Example: limit=20

Page size, 1–100 (default 20).

starting_after
string
Example: starting_after=ch_test_2a3b4c5d6e7f80910a1b2c3d

A cursor — the id of the last object on the previous page. Returns the next page (older) items.

created_from
string <date-time>
Example: created_from=2026-11-04T00:00:00Z

Only objects created at or after this instant. RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC. With created_before it forms a half-open window, so created_from=2026-11-04&created_before=2026-11-05 is exactly that UTC day, and consecutive windows never count an object twice.

created_before
string <date-time>
Example: created_before=2026-11-05T00:00:00Z

Only objects created strictly before this instant. RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC.

status
string
Enum: "pending" "paid" "expired" "cancelled"
Example: status=pending

Only charges in this state.

reference
string <= 100 characters
Example: reference=order_1042

Only the charge carrying this merchant reference.

Responses

Cancel a charge

Cancels a pending charge so it can no longer be paid. Only a pending charge can be cancelled; any other state returns 409 charge_not_pending. Emits charge.cancelled. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Simulate payment (test mode)

Test mode only. Marks a pending charge as paid, exactly as a real customer payment would, and emits charge.paid. Use it to exercise your webhook and fulfilment flow without moving crypto. Any non-pending charge returns 409 charge_not_pending. Requires an Idempotency-Key header. (The same effect is available to a human tester via the "Simulate payment" button on the hosted pay page.)

Payment links

A reusable link. Each visitor who opens it gets a fresh charge; shareable and payable many times.

Create a payment link

Creates a reusable link. Each visitor who opens the link's url gets a fresh charge and is redirected to its hosted pay page, so one link can be shared on social media or printed as a QR code and paid many times. Optionally cap it with max_uses.

A link has no reference or customer (those belong on individual charges) — sending either returns 400 invalid_parameter. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
header Parameters
Idempotency-Key
required
string <= 255 characters
Example: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-a0b1-c2d3e4f50617

A unique key you generate (e.g. a UUID v4), up to 255 characters. Required on every POST that creates or changes something. Retry a failed request with the same key to replay the original response instead of acting twice.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
amount
required
number > 0

Price per charge, in major units of currency (same bounds as a charge's amount).

required
string
Enum: "NGN" "USD"
pay_asset
string
Default: "USDT"
Enum: "USDT" "USDC" "BTC"
pay_network
string
Enum: "trc20" "bep20" "bitcoin"

Must be valid for pay_asset (see CreateChargeRequest).

description
string <= 500 characters
max_uses
integer [ 1 .. 1000000 ]

Cap the number of charges the link may create. Omit for unlimited.

object (Metadata) <= 20 properties

Up to 20 key/value pairs you attach to an object; echoed back on reads and in webhooks. Keys match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$. Values are stored as strings (numbers and booleans are coerced to strings) of at most 500 characters.

Sub-accounts

The tenant layer: your own end-users, provisioned under your business. Sandbox identities only today — a sub-account holds no wallet and accepts no real money (see sandbox).

Create a sub-account

Provisions one of your own end-users under your business — the tenant layer. The sub-account is a sandbox identity: it has no wallet, no balance, and cannot receive real money (the response always says so in sandbox). Live provisioning opens only with the live rails, and this endpoint stays test-mode until then.

name is required. reference is yours (an id from your system) and must be unique within your business; if you omit it, the sub-account id is used. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

bearerAuth

Idempotency-Key

string <= 255 characters

A unique key you generate (e.g. a UUID v4), up to 255 characters. Required on every POST that creates or changes something. Retry a failed request with the same key to replay the original response instead of acting twice.

required
string [ 1 .. 100 ] characters

The sub-account's display name.

email

string [ 1 .. 100 ] characters

Your id for this tenant. Must be unique within your business.

object (Metadata) <= 20 properties

Up to 20 key/value pairs you attach to an object; echoed back on reads and in webhooks. Keys match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}$. Values are stored as strings (numbers and booleans are coerced to strings) of at most 500 characters.

Cards

USD virtual cards a business issues to its own customers, funded and spent through your API. In test mode the whole lifecycle is real in shape and nothing is real in money: no PAN is issued, no issuer is contacted, and no test balance can become spendable. A live key is answered leg by leg rather than with one blanket refusal, because the rails are not all missing at the same rate. Listing, retrieval, freeze and unfreeze run live today — freeze and unfreeze ask the issuer first and only then move our own record, so an issuer that refuses leaves the card active and answers 503 service_unavailable. Issuing, funding, withdrawal, close, spend limits and the transaction list each answer 403 live_precondition_unmet and name the rail they are waiting on in error.param: cardholder, funding, withdrawal, settlement, limit_format or transaction_sync. A param of provider is about your card row, not a rail: that live row carries no issuer id, or an issuer this server has no card code for. The authorization simulator stays test-only under every key — a live authorization is decided by the issuer, not by us. No live leg moves money yet.

Create a virtual card

Issues one sandbox USD card to one of your customers. The card starts at balance: 0 with no spend limits, and every later call on this surface moves or gates that balance.

customer.first_name, customer.last_name and customer.email are required; the customer is validated and then not stored — no name or email is persisted on the card, so a leaked card id carries no PII with it. reference is yours, unique per business (a repeat returns 409 duplicate_reference), and defaults to the card id. currency may only be USD; sending anything else returns 400.

The three limits are optional at issue time and are set or cleared later on POST /cards/{id}/spend_limits. They are per-card ceilings you choose, and no platform maximum is applied to any single axis. FirstFlip's ceilings sit elsewhere: one on how many cards a key may hold open, and one on what all your cards may spend together — both stated below and in the authorization section.

FirstFlip's one cap on issuing is a count, not an amount: a key may hold 250 open cards. The 251st POST /cards answers 409 card_limit_reached with param: cards and nothing moves; closing a card frees a slot, so a healthy integration is never locked out. Resending the same Idempotency-Key is not a new card and is not counted.

The response shows number_last4, expiry_month and expiry_year. Those are minted here for shape only — this card has no issuer, no full PAN and no CVV, and sandbox.real_card says so on every answer. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Live mode: a live key is refused here before the body is read — issuing a real card needs the cardholder rail FirstFlip has not built, so this answers 403 live_precondition_unmet with param: cardholder. No card is minted, and the refusal is what your key replays.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
header Parameters
Idempotency-Key
required
string <= 255 characters
Example: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-a0b1-c2d3e4f50617

A unique key you generate (e.g. a UUID v4), up to 255 characters. Required on every POST that creates or changes something. Retry a failed request with the same key to replay the original response instead of acting twice.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
currency
string

Optional, and only ever USD. Anything else is 400 invalid_parameter rather than a fallback.

Value: "USD"
reference
string <= 100 characters

Your id for this card. Unique per key and mode; defaults to the generated id. A second attempt with the same reference and a different Idempotency-Key answers 409 duplicate_reference.

required
object

Who the card is for. Only these three fields are accepted, and nothing about the customer is stored — the same rule virtual accounts hold. Names and emails live in your database; the card carries your reference so you can join them back.

daily_limit
number or null >= 0.01

Rolling-24h authorization ceiling in major units. Omit or null for no ceiling.

per_transaction_limit
number or null >= 0.01

Largest single authorization in major units. Omit or null for no ceiling.

monthly_limit
number or null >= 0.01

Rolling-30-day authorization ceiling in major units. Omit or null for no ceiling.

Responses

Sandbox (test mode). The only base URL available today; the entire /v1 surface is test-mode and moves no money. Live mode is not yet enabled.

https://api.firstflip.ng/v1/cards

Retrieve a virtual card

Returns one card, including its current balance, status and limits. This is the read your own UI should render from — never from a value cached after a write, because a spend can have landed since.

Live mode: this read runs live. A live card answers livemode: true with sandbox: null; a card belonging to the other mode is a 404, byte-for-byte the answer for a card that does not exist.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
id

Fund a virtual card

Puts money on the card from your business's sandbox funding, and returns the ledger row that describes the credit (type: topup, status: completed, with balance_before and balance_after). The row and the balance move in one commit, so a funding row can never describe money the card did not receive.

Funding a frozen card is allowed — money arriving is never blocked by a freeze, only money leaving. Funding a closed card returns 409 card_closed. Requires an Idempotency-Key header: retry the same key to replay this credit instead of funding twice.

Live mode: refused — funding needs a tenant USD balance to move money from, and that rail is not built. This answers 403 live_precondition_unmet with param: funding before your amount is read.

Withdraw from a virtual card

Takes money back off the card (type: withdrawal, status: completed). The same commit rule as funding applies: row and balance move together.

A withdrawal is refused with 409 card_not_active unless the card is active — a freeze stops money leaving, and a close stops everything (409 card_closed). An amount larger than the balance returns 400 insufficient_balance with param: amount, and nothing moves. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Live mode: refused — taking real money off a card needs the withdrawal rail, and FirstFlip has not proved that provider verb yet. This answers 403 live_precondition_unmet with param: withdrawal before your amount is read.

Freeze a virtual card

Stops the card from spending or being withdrawn from, and keeps every other property — the balance, the limits, the id — exactly as they are. reason (max 200 chars) is stored and returned as frozen_reason.

Freezing is idempotent by outcome: freezing an already-frozen card answers 200 with that state rather than an error, so two racing requests cannot disagree. A closed card answers 409 card_closed. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Live mode: this leg runs live, and it is the leg that matters on the day a card is reported lost.

Unfreeze a virtual card

Returns a frozen card to active and clears frozen_reason. A frozen card keeps its balance, so unfreezing restores spending without funding it again.

A closed card cannot be reopened — 409 card_closed says to issue a new one. Unfreezing a card that is already active answers 200 with its current state. Requires an Idempotency-Key header. No request body is read.

Live mode: this leg runs live with the same ordering as freeze — the issuer releases the card first, and our record follows only if it agrees. A refusing issuer answers 503 service_unavailable and the card stays frozen.

Close a virtual card

Ends the card for good, from either active or frozen. reason (max 200 chars) is stored and returned as closed_reason.

Close is terminal: every later write against the card answers 409 card_closed, and the card cannot be reopened — issue a new one. Closing an already-closed card answers 200. Any balance still on the card is left as recorded against it and is not paid out by this call; withdraw it first if the money must come back. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Live mode: refused — closing a real card has to settle whatever is outstanding against it, and the settlement rail is not built. This answers 403 live_precondition_unmet with param: settlement and changes nothing, on either side.

Update a card's spend limits

Sets the merchant-side ceilings an authorization is judged against. Send at least one of daily_limit, per_transaction_limit or monthly_limit; the axes you leave out are left alone, and an explicit null clears that axis (no ceiling).

daily_limit and monthly_limit are rolling windows — 24 hours and 30 days from now, not a calendar day or month — and they are summed from the committed approvals at the moment the spend lands, not from a read taken earlier. That is what makes the ceiling hold when thirty authorizations arrive at once. per_transaction_limit is a single-authorization maximum and is checked before either window. Requires an Idempotency-Key header.

Live mode: refused — the issuer has rejected every amount format this platform has tried on that call, and a ceiling sent in the wrong unit is worse than none. Writing it only on our side would be a limit a live card does not actually obey, so this answers 403 live_precondition_unmet with param: limit_format.

Simulate a card authorization

The stand-in for a live purchase, and the only way to see an approval or a decline on this surface. An approved authorization is the debit: the ledger row (type: authorization, status: approved) and the balance drop commit together. A declined one writes the row with status: declined and a decline_code, and moves no money.

The decline reason is decided in this order: card_frozen, over_per_transaction_limit, over_daily_limit, over_monthly_limit, over_tenant_monthly_limit, insufficient_funds. Code your retry logic against those six — a frozen card and an over-limit card are different customer conversations, and insufficient_funds is the one a top-up fixes. over_tenant_monthly_limit is the only one of the six that is not yours to set: it is a ceiling FirstFlip places on what all of your cards may spend in a rolling 30 days ($1,000,000 of approved authorization spend per business).

Every answer is 201: a decline is a recorded outcome of a real request, not a failed one. A closed card is the exception and answers 409 card_closed. Requires an Idempotency-Key header — the same key cannot approve and decline two different attempts.

Live mode: refused with 403 live_mode_unavailable, and this is the one leg that will stay that way.

List a card's transactions

The card's own ledger, newest first: every credit, withdrawal and authorization attempt, approved or declined. This is the reconciliation source — the rows sum to the card's balance, and a declined row carries the decline_code that explains it.

Filter by type (topup, withdrawal, authorization) and/or status (completed, approved, declined), by a created_from/created_before window, and page with limit plus starting_after.

Live mode: refused — the rows behind a live card are the issuer's, and they are not synced into this platform yet. An empty list would read as "this card has spent nothing", which is a guess, so this answers 403 live_precondition_unmet with param: transaction_sync.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
id
required
string
Example: card_test_3a4b5c6d7e8f90122a3b4c5d

The card id (card_test_…) returned when the card was issued.

query Parameters
limit
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 20
Example: limit=20

Page size, 1–100 (default 20).

starting_after
string
Example: starting_after=ch_test_2a3b4c5d6e7f80910a1b2c3d

A cursor — the id of the last object on the previous page. Returns the next page (older) items.

created_from
string <date-time>
Example: created_from=2026-11-04T00:00:00Z

Only objects created at or after this instant. RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC. With created_before it forms a half-open window, so created_from=2026-11-04&created_before=2026-11-05 is exactly that UTC day, and consecutive windows never count an object twice.

created_before
string <date-time>
Example: created_before=2026-11-05T00:00:00Z

Only objects created strictly before this instant. RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC.

type
string
Enum: "topup" "withdrawal" "authorization"
Example: type=authorization

Only rows of this kind.

status
string
Enum: "completed" "approved" "declined"
Example: status=declined

Only rows in this final state.

Responses

Sandbox (test mode). The only base URL available today; the entire /v1 surface is test-mode and moves no money. Live mode is not yet enabled.

https://api.firstflip.ng/v1/cards/{id}/transactions

Assistant

A documentation Q&A helper that answers only from the published FirstFlip docs.

Ask the developer assistant

Answers a developer question strictly from the published FirstFlip documentation (it never invents facts; unsupported claims are scrubbed, and removed_claims counts how many). This is not a money call and takes no Idempotency-Key. Rate limited to 30 questions per key per hour. The assistant is gated by a separate switch and is OFF by default; when off it returns 503 assistant_disabled.

Hosted pages

Public, browser-facing pages (the token in the URL is the capability — no secret key). These return HTML, not JSON. In test mode the pay page carries a "Simulate payment" button.

The browser-facing page a customer opens (this is a charge's hosted_url). Shows the quote and, while the charge is pending, a "Simulate payment" button. The token is the capability; no secret key is used. Returns HTML.

token
required
string^[0-9a-f]{32}$

List test transfers

Newest first, limit 1–100 (default 20). Filter by status, by the batch_id that created the payout, or by a created_from / created_before window. Page with starting_after set to the last id of the previous page, and stop when has_more is false.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
limit
integer [ 1 .. 100 ]
Default: 20
Example: limit=20
starting_after
string <= 100 characters
Example: starting_after=tr_test_3c4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7
status
string
Enum: "new" "pending" "successful" "failed"
Example: status=successful
batch_id
string <= 100 characters
Example: batch_id=trb_test_4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8
created_from
string <date-time>
Example: created_from=2026-11-04T00:00:00Z

Only transfers created at or after this instant. RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC. With created_before it forms a half-open window, so consecutive windows never count a transfer twice.

created_before
string <date-time>
Example: created_before=2026-11-05T00:00:00Z

Only transfers created strictly before this instant. RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC.

Responses

Sandbox (test mode). The only base URL available today; the entire /v1 surface is test-mode and moves no money. Live mode is not yet enabled.

Webhooks

Deliveries to your endpoint, signed with FirstFlip-Signature. Verify over the raw body and deduplicate on FirstFlip-Event-Id; any non-2xx or timeout is retried with backoff.

A charge was paid Webhook

Sent when a charge transitions to paid. data.object is the full Charge with status: "paid" and a paid_at. This is the event to fulfil an order on. Delivery is at-least-once and deduplicated by event id; return any 2xx quickly to acknowledge.

Verify every webhook over the RAW body before parsing it. The FirstFlip-Signature header is t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex> where v1 = HMAC-SHA256(signingSecret, "<t>.<rawBody>"). Recompute it with your endpoint's signing secret (whsec_…, shown once at registration), compare in constant time, and reject if t is more than 300 seconds from now (replay guard).

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
header Parameters
FirstFlip-Signature
required
string
Example: t=1762000496,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa5f9f6e3b0c0e3f1d2a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6

t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(signingSecret, "<t>.<rawBody>")>. Verify over the raw body.

FirstFlip-Event-Id
required
string

The event id (evt_…). Use it to deduplicate at-least-once deliveries.

FirstFlip-Event-Type
required
string

The event type, e.g. charge.paid.

Request Body schema: application/json
required
id
required
string

Unique event id (evt_…).

object
required
string
Value: "event"
type
required
string
Enum: "charge.paid" "charge.expired" "charge.cancelled" "fx.quote.processing" "fx.quote.ready" "fx.quote.expired" "fx.quote.failed" "fx.trade.pending" "fx.trade.settled" "fx.trade.failed" "virtual_account.payment.successful" "virtual_account.payment.failed" "virtual_account.payment.reversed" "bvn.verified" "bvn.declined" "bvn.failed" "transfer.pending" "transfer.successful" "transfer.failed" "card.created" "card.funded" "card.withdrawn" "card.frozen" "card.unfrozen" "card.closed" "card.limits.updated" "card.authorization.approved" "card.authorization.declined"

The event type.

livemode
required
boolean

Always false today.

created_at
required
string <date-time>
required
object

The event payload.
